translations.text: [?] they dispute in doubt [?] the Son of God. Thus indeed said the prophet: "[?] to his [?] whom you seek, whom you desire."
that he is born of the Father, is named the Son of God, [?] is read [?] to be announced beforehand, [?] the same Father foretold [?], saying:
"and [bring] you to the place which I have prepared. [?] him, [?] do not sin against him."
Who then is this angel [?] ruling [?] for the Lord God among all the sons of God? He indeed is the Son, who, ever sent from the Father, afterward showed himself again to the sight of men.
From that same sending he is named angel.

Isaiah also more openly confirmed that same Son born of the Father, when he said: "The voice of the Lord repaying recompense to his enemies," signifying that same Jewish people who do not believe. Thus also said the prophet:
"Before she was in labor she gave birth, and before her time came she bore a male child."
Thus the same prophet said openly: Before the virgin bore Christ in the flesh,

the Father begot the Son in his divinity; and before the virgin's time came to give birth, the Father begot him without any beginning of time. About this the prophet said afterward: "Who has ever heard, or who has ever seen anything like this, anything at all among men that is in any way like it?"
And afterward he said: "Shall I, who make others give birth, not give birth myself? said the Lord.
"And shall I, who give others to bear, be barren?" With all this testimony it is [?]
[for him] who does not believe, that he choose one of two things: either to believe Christ the Son of God, or [to hold] false the prophets who foretold this.
OF THIS IT SPEAKS HERE: HOW CHRIST WAS BORN INEFFABLY OF THE FATHER BEFORE CREATION.
Many are seeking
at what time the Son of God was born,
and he is ever-existing, just as it is written of him: "His going forth [?]
"nor yet the circuit of the earth of the world.
When he made ready the heavens, there was I; when with a firm law he enclosed the waters of the abyss round about, when he weighed the foundations of the earth,
I was with him then, making all this."
By the testimony of such great authority it is now so openly declared that Christ the Son of God was born of the Father before all ages.

It is now made known, then, that everything that is created came to be from the almighty Father through him. But as to what they now seek anew, how this same one was born: in his holy birth there is so hidden a mystery of the Father that no apostle tells it, nor did any prophet discover it, nor did any angel of God know it, nor did any creature come to understand it.
Isaiah confirmed this where he said: "Who shall declare Christ's birth?"
Therefore now, if the prophet of God could not declare Christ's birth, who will presume to understand how the Son could be born of the Father?
About this same thing it is also said in the books of Job: "Where do you find the wisdom of the divine Father? It is hidden from the eyes of men, and it is concealed from all that fly in heaven."
It is indeed unknown even to the angels themselves.
"This the Lord said to my Christ the Lord." And it is now beyond doubt and plain to understand that this is said in the name of our Lord.
If Christ is not God, let the unbelievers now tell us to whom God was speaking in Genesis, where he said: "Let us make man in our image and in our likeness."

As is also said there afterwards: "And God created man; in the image and likeness of God he made him." Let them now ask again which God created him, or in whose divinity he made in his image the man whom he created.
If they answer and say "in that of the angels":
But surely an angel is not equal to God?

There is so very great a difference between the likeness of the creature and that of the one who created everything. Or could an angel make man just as God did? Believing that would be great madness. So to whom is this said, or in whose likeness was man created, if not in the likeness of the one
who is equal to God and bears the same name as God?
And again, if Christ is not Lord, which Lord rained fire on Sodom from the Lord?
As it is certainly written in Genesis: "And the Lord rained brimstone and fire from the Lord upon Sodom and Gomorrah."

In this saying let no one doubt that this is certainly the second person of God, the Lord Christ himself. And who then is that Lord, if not truly the Son from the Father? He was always sent from the Father and used to come down from heaven and go back up.
This testimony shows in clearer light both the one divinity and the distinction between the two persons, Father and Son.
But if Christ is not Lord, about whom did David say in the Psalms: "The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand"?
Although Christ, in the body of the flesh, is David's son, yet in the Holy Spirit he is certainly God and Lord.
If Christ were not Lord, about whom did David say in the Books of Kings:
"Thus said the man to whom it was granted, the noble psalmist of Israel, concerning the Christ of the God of Jacob: The Spirit of the Lord speaks through me, and his word through my tongue"?
Now if Christ is not Lord, who is the Lord of hosts who was sent by the Lord of hosts?
As he himself said through Zechariah: "Thus said the Lord God of hosts: He sent me after glory to the nations that plundered you.

Whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye. See, therefore I lift my hand over them, and they will become plunder for those who once served them, and you will know that the Lord of hosts sent me."

Truly, whose voice can this be if not the voice of the saving Lord? He, almighty God, declared that he was sent by the almighty Father. He was indeed sent to the nations according to the glory of his divinity, which he shared with the Father. When he emptied himself and took the form of a servant, he became obedient even unto death.
The same one, also, said in what follows here:
"Praise and rejoice,
…daughter of Zion, because see, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst,
says the Lord.
And on that day many nations will be gathered to the Lord and will become my people, and I will dwell in your midst,
and you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you."
Who, then, is this Lord who is sent by the Lord of hosts, if not that same Lord, the Saviour Christ?
Beyond that, it was also said here before concerning the Holy Spirit, concerning his divinity, and that he is the Spirit of God.
Job spoke thus: "The Spirit of the Lord made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life.

See, God made me just as he made you." Concerning that same Spirit he had certainly said before: "The Spirit of the Lord made me." He then joined that to God when he said afterwards: "See, God made me just as he made you."
By this he made known that this same Spirit is God.
HERE IT SPEAKS OF THE INDICATION OF THE THREE PERSONS OF GOD

It is shown in the books of the old law that the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are God. But the Jewish people do not believe that the Son and the Holy Spirit are God, because they heard God's voice loudly on Mount Sinai, saying:
"Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God is one God."
They do not understand how in the Trinity there is one God, Father and Son and Holy Spirit. They are not three gods at all; rather, in these three persons there is one name of the undivided power.

Let us now seek this same Trinity in the old holy scripture. In the first part of the books of Kings it is certainly written thus: "David the son of Jesse said, the man said, to whom it was proclaimed concerning the Christ of the God of Jacob, the excellent singer of Israel: The Spirit of God speaks through me, and his word goes forth through my tongue." And immediately afterwards he showed openly who the Spirit is, when he said:
"The God of Israel spoke to me, the righteous ruler of men, the strong one of Israel."

Where he said "the Christ of the God of Jacob," he certainly meant the Son and the Father. And where he said "The Spirit of God speaks through me," he meant there, clearly recognizable, the Holy Spirit.
Again, David also spoke of this same thing in the Psalms: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the spirit of his mouth all their power stands."
In the name of the Lord we certainly recognize the Father; in the Word we believe in the Son. In the spirit of his mouth we certainly understand the Holy Spirit.
In this testimony the number of the Trinity and the communion of their single work are truly shown.
As the same prophet said hereafter:

"He sends his word and melts them; his spirit breathes, and the waters flow." See, here he now means three: the Father is the one who sent, and the Word is what was sent, and his Spirit is the one who breathes.
And also in Genesis it says: "In the beginning God made heaven and earth, and the Spirit of God hovered over the waters."
There, too, the Father is to be understood in the name of God; in "the beginning" the Son is to be recognized, because he himself said:

"At the head of the book it is written of me, that I should do your will." God is the one who spoke, and God is the one who acted. And moreover, in that he hovered over the waters, he signified the Holy Spirit there.

So also, certainly, where God said, "Let us make man in our image and likeness": through the plurality of the persons the sign of the Trinity is revealed there. And yet, so that he might show the oneness of God, he said immediately afterward: "God made man in his own image." And again, where God said afterward, "Behold, Adam has become like one of us": this same plurality in the naming shows the mighty mystery of the Trinity.
The prophet Haggai showed the holy mystery of this same Trinity in this way, speaking in the Lord's name: "My Spirit shall be in the midst among you."

Behold, God spoke there; behold, his Spirit is also meant immediately after. Concerning the third person, who is the Son, the same prophet said this: "For behold, I will shake heaven and earth, and the one desired by all nations shall come."

In the same way, the distinct difference of each of the persons is also shown in the books of Isaiah, where the Son of God himself says: "I am the first and I am the last. My hands also made the earth, and my right hand measured the heavens.
And from the beginning I was speaking in secret, from time; and before any time came to be, I was there."
Immediately after that he also said: "And now the Lord God and his Spirit have sent me."
Behold here two of the persons,
God and his Spirit, who did the sending; and the third person is that of the Lord Christ himself, the one who was sent.

So also, in another place, the sign of the Trinity was shown through the same holy prophet in this way: "God said: Behold my servant, I will receive him; my beloved, my soul is well pleased in him. I have put my Spirit upon him." There the Father meant his Son when he named the beloved servant upon whom he put his Spirit.
Concerning this Spirit, the Lord Christ the Savior testified with his own voice when he said: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me."
And in another place Isaiah himself also took in the whole Trinity by a counting of fingers, when he preached and said:
"Who measured the water in a single handful? And who weighed the heavens with his palm? Who weighed the whole globe of the earth with three fingers?"

Indeed, by the three fingers the holy prophet weighed the threefold coequality of the almighty Godhead on the scale of a certain mystery. And also, through the equality of might, he made known by the three fingers the power of their working together and the oneness of the almighty effectiveness, which is one and the same in the Trinity.

In another place the same prophet also made known that he recognized the mystery of the Trinity, when he said this: "I saw the Lord sitting on a very high throne, and the seraphim, the angels, stood above him.
First, the name of Jesus was found, signified beforehand in prefigurations of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For that reason indeed Hoshea the son of Nun was named by Moses with the name Jesus.
This same man received the lordship of the people of Israel when he became its leader after the death of Moses and divided among them the lands of the inheritance promised to them.
What did the change of name signify? Only that, after Moses was dead and the law had passed away and the old commandments of God had ceased, our Lord Jesus Christ was to become our leader,

who, having sanctified us through the stream of the Jordan, that is, through the gift of holy baptism, with all kinds of sins driven out and all the hosts of evil angels put to flight, leads us through into the promised land,
where honey and milk flow, that is, into the riches of eternal life, for nothing is sweeter than that.
Therefore indeed the son of Nun received the likeness of the holy mystery, in that he was named Jesus as a prefiguration of the true Jesus. Concerning him it is written in the Psalms:
"Come and let us praise the Lord; let us sing with shouting to God our Jesus."
Here it is shown that Jesus is the Lord, concerning whom it also says in another place in the Psalms:
"The Lord takes pleasure in his people, and he raises up the meek in Jesus." This is indeed said in this way in the Hebrew scripture.
HOW OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST ALSO CAME FROM THE SEED OF ABRAHAM.
Genesis tells what Abraham's command to his servant was:
"Put your hand under my thigh and swear by the God of heaven." In these words he proclaimed beforehand concerning Christ, the heavenly Lord, that he was to come in the flesh of his lineage.

By the thigh is indeed to be understood offspring. It thus signified that the heavenly God was to come in the flesh from the seed of Abraham. In his seed it was promised to him by the Lord, through Isaiah, saying:
"In your seed all nations shall be blessed," that is, in Christ.
Of him the psalmist said: "And in him all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed; all nations shall praise him."
And concerning that seed the voice of the Lord said through the same Isaiah: "I will bring forth from the seed of Jacob, and from Judah, him who shall possess my mountains."
Concerning this also, in another place, the same prophet said: "Unless the Lord had left us seed."
AND WHY CHRIST WAS AWAITED IN THE FLESH OF THE TRIBE OF JUDAH.
Jacob the patriarch said prophetically:
"A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs,
until he comes who is to be sent, and he himself is the expectation of the nations." It is indeed true that, until the coming of Christ's birth,

the Jewish people did not remain without rulers from the tribe of Judah, nor without a leader from his thighs, until Herod, the foreign king. He, in desire for the kingdom, through the seizure [?] of power [?].
As soon as this was done, and leadership from the seed of Judah then ceased, and he came who was to be sent,

for whom nations and peoples were waiting. The Jews, however, in their fierceness and with the shameless face they have, say falsely that the time is not yet fulfilled, [claiming that] some king or other of the lineage of Judah is ruling in the farthest ends of the east.
Blind in mind, they take no notice that their false lies have been exposed. For just as no temple remains to them anymore, nor any altar, nor any sacrificial offering,
so likewise no king and no priest remains to them, the Jewish people.

Nor can the prophet Hosea be lying in any way, who said through the Holy Spirit: "The sons of Israel shall sit without king, without lord, without sacrificial offering, without altar, without priesthood, without revelations."
Who is there who does not see all this now fulfilled in them?
HERE IT TELLS HOW CHRIST WAS BORN OF DAVID'S DESCENT
Let us now see from what lineage Christ was to be born: that he was to come from David's descent according to the measure of the flesh, through the Holy Spirit,
as was foretold of him in the Psalms: "The Lord swore to David in truth and did not deceive him: I will set the fruit of your womb upon my throne."
"Once I swore by my holiness:
I will not lie to David; his seed shall dwell forever. And his throne is like the sun before my face, and forever like the full-grown moon,
and he is the faithful witness in heaven."
So also in another place it is written in Paralipomenon:
"And the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying: Go and say to my servant David:
Thus said the Lord: I tell you that the Lord will build you a house. When you have fulfilled your days, so that you go to your forefathers,
I will raise up your seed after you, who shall be from among your sons,
and I will establish his kingdom. He himself shall build me a house, and I will make his seat firm forever.
I shall be to him in the place of a father, and he shall be to me in the place of a son, and I will not take my mercy from him as I took it from the one
who was before you.
And I will establish him in my house and in my kingdom unto everlasting eternity. And his throne shall be most firm forever."
Whoever thinks that all this was fulfilled in Solomon understands it very wrongly. For how can what was said here be understood of Solomon: "After you sleep with your fathers,
I will raise up your seed after you, who shall be from among your sons,
and I will establish his kingdom for him"? It is by no means to be believed that this was foretold of that Solomon,
who indeed began to reign while his father was still living.
But here it says:
"For when your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed."
From this it is to be understood that another was promised there, for he was not foretold to be raised up before David's death, but after his death.
Concerning him the Lord himself said through Jeremiah:

"Behold, the days are coming, said the Lord, when I will raise up for David a righteous offspring, and a king shall then reign, and he will be wise and will carry out judgment and justice on the earth.
In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel too shall dwell in confidence.
And this is his name, as they shall call him: This is our Lord, the righteous one."
He who was promised through Nathan from the seed of David,
that same one was also foretold through Isaiah the prophet;
he said:
"A rod shall grow up from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up from his root." He said this because he was indeed from the region of Bethlehem, of the lineage of David.
This rod from the root of Jesse is the immaculate virgin Mary, who came forth from the root of David,
who bore the flower,
the saving Lord.
Concerning the same one, this also follows here: "And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and of understanding thought,
the spirit of counsel and of might,
the spirit of knowledge and of mercy,
and the spirit of the fear of God shall fill him."
So many gifts of the Spirit are foretold concerning him because the Holy Spirit does not dwell in him by measure, as it does in us.
Rather, in him is all the fullness of the gifts of God and of the Spirit.
This is he who "does not judge according to the sight of the eyes and the hearing of the ears,
but righteousness is the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness is the belt of his reins."
In his kingdom "the wolf dwells with the lamb," and he who was accustomed to carry off plunder from the church,
once he has been converted, makes his dwelling with the innocent.
In his law "the leopard lies down with the kid": this signifies the malicious mingled with the sinful.
There also "the calf," from the Jewish law,
"the lion," from worldly power, and "the sheep," from the rank of humble people, "dwell together" with the stronger in the church of Christ, because there, in the true faith, all share a common life.
